meta.description: Families are organised by the function they deliver, not by the chapter that describes them. Shaft/hub connections and bearings are expanded; other families start collapsed.
notes: Element types are OWL classes; design alternatives are individuals. Substitution operates on alternatives, never on element classes.
Families are deliberately NOT disjoint: a setscrew both connects and fastens.
meta.title: Machine-element taxonomy (Level 3)

data.definition: A standardised or generically recognised mechanical component type whose design is treated as a self-contained problem with its own selection procedure, failure modes and verification methods.
data.label: Machine Element

data.definition: A non-rotating or torque-free member that supports rotating elements.
data.label: Axle

data.definition: A support element that carries load between members in relative motion.
data.label: Bearing

data.definition: A connection in which a split hub is drawn onto a smooth shaft by screws, gripping it by friction.
data.label: Clamping (Split) Hub Connection

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to join two members so that load or motion passes between them, while defining their relative position.
data.label: Connection Element
data.scopeNote: The pilot family of this ontology version. Its members compete for a single function -- transmit torque between a shaft and a mounted element -- which makes it the clearest setting for substitution reasoning.

data.definition: A connection element joining two shafts end to end to transmit torque.
data.label: Coupling

data.definition: A machine element that stores mechanical energy and returns it in a controlled way.
data.label: Energy Storage Element

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to hold parts together, typically through a preload or a permanent bond, rather than to transmit a working torque.
data.label: Fastening Element
data.scopeNote: Overlaps ConnectionElement by design: a setscrew is both. The families answer different questions and are not partitioned.

data.definition: A power transmission element that spans a centre distance through a flexible tension member.
data.label: Flexible Drive Element

data.definition: A toothed element transmitting power between shafts by conjugate tooth action.
data.label: Gear

data.definition: A taper key with an extended head permitting extraction from the end at which it was installed.
data.label: Gib-Head Key

data.definition: A connection in which torque is carried by friction at an interface pressurised by dimensional interference between shaft and hub.
data.label: Interference-Fit Connection

data.definition: A spline whose tooth flanks are involute curves, as on a gear tooth.
data.label: Involute Spline

data.definition: A separate member seated partly in a shaft groove and partly in a hub groove, carrying torque between them.
data.label: Key

data.definition: A proprietary assembly of tapered rings drawn together by fasteners, which grips a smooth shaft and a hub bore by friction.
data.label: Keyless Locking Assembly
data.scopeNote: Proprietary products are named as element types but their performance data are never asserted here; they require manufacturer data (mdcore:RequiresManufacturerData).

data.definition: A machine element that starts, stops or modulates the transmission of power or the motion of a member.
data.label: Motion Control Element
data.scopeNote: Added beyond the seven families of the original outline because clutches and brakes are functionally distinct from steady power transmission: their defining function is to interrupt or dissipate, not to convey.

data.definition: A machine element that constrains motion to an intended path.
data.label: Motion Guidance Element

data.definition: A key whose top, bottom and sides are parallel; square or rectangular in section.
data.label: Parallel Key

data.definition: A member passing through a transverse hole in both hub and shaft.
data.label: Pin

data.definition: A cylindrical pin seated in matching cylindrical grooves in shaft and hub.
data.label: Pin Key

data.definition: A bearing in which load passes through a sliding interface, with or without a lubricant film.
data.label: Plain (Sliding) Bearing

data.definition: A screw used to convert rotation into translation under load.
data.label: Power Screw

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to convey mechanical power between locations, optionally changing speed, torque or direction.
data.label: Power Transmission Element

data.definition: An interference fit assembled by axial force at ambient temperature.
data.label: Press-Fit Connection

data.definition: A ring seated in a groove to locate a component axially.
data.label: Retaining Ring

data.definition: A bearing in which load passes through rolling elements between raceways.
data.label: Rolling-Contact Bearing

data.definition: A machine element that restricts the passage of fluid or contaminant across an interface.
data.label: Sealing Element

data.definition: A threaded member tightened through the hub against the shaft, developing holding power by compression.
data.label: Setscrew

data.definition: A rotating member that carries power-transmitting elements and transmits torque along its axis.
data.label: Shaft

data.definition: A connection element occupying the interface between a shaft and the bore of a mounted power-transmitting element.
data.label: Shaft/Hub Connection Element

data.definition: A pin deliberately sized to fail at a chosen overload, so as to protect costlier parts of the mechanism.
data.label: Shear Pin
data.scopeNote: Its defining function is mech:LimitTransmittedTorque, not mech:TransmitTorqueShaftToHub alone. Replacing a shear pin with a stronger connection removes a required function.

data.definition: An interference fit assembled by differential thermal expansion.
data.label: Shrink-Fit Connection

data.definition: A set of axial teeth or keys formed integrally on a shaft, engaging matching grooves in the bore of the mating part.
data.label: Spline

data.definition: A rolled, split tubular pin retained by its own spring force in an undersized hole.
data.label: Split Tubular Spring Pin

data.definition: A machine element that carries reaction loads while permitting an intended relative motion, or that provides a structural seat for other elements.
data.label: Support Element

data.definition: A key with a tapered top surface, driven in from the end of the hub after the hub is in position.
data.label: Taper Key

data.definition: A connection in which a tapered shaft end and a matching hub bore are drawn together, commonly by a nut on a threaded shaft end.
data.label: Tapered-Fit Connection

data.definition: A segment-of-a-circle key seated in a circular shaft groove.
data.label: Woodruff Key
